random_sample.note: time-boxed: picks until the next pass is due (priority tiers, then the week's quarter); see sample.py
random_sample.host_weights_note: new apps a day when sampling (2026-11-01 estimate): primaries ~8 (631) / ~16 (629) after canaries and the update path, sample-only hosts ~50; re-set from real speed after a week; pool = each pool slot (a GitHub macOS runner, 2026-11-04: guessed at 636's speed); 2026-11-15: 858 (macOS) and 861 (Windows) became the primaries, 631/636/624/629/635 went to standby (FMA_SOAK_STANDBY_*); their weights stay for when one is scheduled again

priority._doc: sample.py: priority apps get a real lifecycle cycle at least every every_hours (any host; most overdue first, hosts rotate per period). slack_hours: a pass may take an app that much early; grace_hours: how late counts as on time in the digest. update (runner.update_due): a priority title's update path runs on a new release, a new Fleet build (new_build_tiers) and every every_days; keep_tiers' titles stay in the soak fleet (titles.py) so Fleet caches the older version the update path needs. Only the twice_daily tier is kept: keeping daily too would store ~15 GB more installers on qa's filesystem store, which filled up once (#57132). The lists are maintained by hand.

alternate._doc: sample.tier_host: the listed tiers take each platform's host groups in turn, one group per period, so every app runs on each OS build; host IDs as in FMA_SOAK_HOST_*.

quarters._doc: sample.py: every non-priority app has a fixed quarter (crc32 of the slug % count); weeks since epoch (a Monday) pick the quarter, so the whole catalog runs every count weeks (2: twice a month, from 2026-11-15 when the soak went to 3 macOS and 5 Windows hosts).

winget_ignore._doc: audit 1.11-1.13 (winget_health.py) hits reviewed as false alarms, per check: slug -> why. Reviewed 2026-11-16 on the first full sweep.

arch._doc: Hosts by CPU. Routing (sample.py): a Windows app whose slug ends in -arm64 (name ends in "(ARM64)", ~25 apps) runs only on the arm64 hosts; other Windows apps go to the x64 hosts, except the tiers in priority.alternate, which cover every OS build on purpose. Triage (digest.arch_policy): an x64 app's failure on an arm64 host is never filed (Prism emulation is best-effort: some install but won't launch, like firefox@nightly, some installers refuse ARM); crosshost.py reruns it on an x64 host and only a failure there is a bug. An -arm64 app's failure on an x64 host is never filed; only a failure on an arm64 host is. Hosts on neither list get normal triage. Standby hosts are listed so their crosshost reruns follow the same rules. Policy set 2026-11-17.

watcher.residents_note: 2026-11-11: asana/windows replaced aws-cli/windows. AWS CLI's patch policy always passes (#56971), so its transitions could never fire, and as a resident it never got a lifecycle cycle (the last Windows app uncovered). Asana: 11 catalog versions in 30 days, clean lifecycle on 629.

skip.swiftdialog/darwin: quits on its own when opened with no content, before and after the install, on all 4 Macs (2026-11-05)

stuck._doc: stuck.py: a queue whose oldest activity waited this long is stuck; restart_hosts get an MDM restart (max per day), others only an alert. 635 is the physical NucBox people use (it hosts the findings VM): alert only.

disk._doc: disk.py: a soak host below min_gb free alerts once ("Soak host low on disk" issue); it clears once back above min_gb + hysteresis_gb.

held._doc: held.py: once a day, quarantine entries and harness leftovers held this many days go to the "Soak items held over 3 days" issue.

replace_preexisting._doc: runner.py: when an app is already on the host and the harness didn't install it, uninstall it with the FMA's uninstall script and test the FMA (Brayan, 2026-11-05). Otherwise the cycle is skipped. except_hosts: hosts where existing apps are never removed (635 is the physical NucBox people use). keep: slugs never removed (fleetd's own Desktop).

allow._doc: except_hosts exceptions: apps that may be replaced there anyway, approved by Brayan 2026-11-08 to complete the catalog. Reinstalled at the catalog version when the cycle ends (runner.restore).

recheck.note: closed FMA catalog bugs rerun on the host that found them, at least settle_minutes after the close (fixes ship ~1 h after merge); recheck.py
recheck.label: ~fma-soak

title_cleanup._doc: titles.py sweep (report job, after every soak and pool job): removes the soak's FMA titles from the soak fleet so stored installers don't fill the instance's disk (#57132 on qa.fleetdm.com, 2026-11-06). keep_title_ids: titles Brayan added before the soak (fleet 65 activity log, 2026-11-07); canaries, residents, patch_closed apps, apps still on a host and queued titles are kept by rule.

coverage._doc: sample.py: a lifecycle cycle started inside an invalid window that didn't pass doesn't count as coverage, so the app goes back to catch-up for a clean run. Times are local, like records.

invalid_windows.why: qa installer store full (#57132): adds 500 'no space left', installs 'image not recognized'

rerun._doc: sample.py: these apps go first, once each, until one has a lifecycle cycle started after `since` (local time, like records). 2026-11-07: apps whose only failures came from qa's full installer store (#57132) with errors a wrong install script also gives, and no clean install before it; yacreader/windows had non-install findings in a broken run. Triage marked them environment (triage.json); a clean run proves it, a failure comes back as a new finding. 35 of 37 ran 2026-11-07 (34 clean or flaky-uninstall only; goldendict-ng/windows a new finding); mist and shifty were skipped (pool host missed the presence query), queued again and passed 2026-11-08 00:46/00:56. 2026-11-08: grammarly-desktop/darwin (host-specific relaunch failure on 636). 2026-11-08 22:45: zoom-rooms/darwin (one unexplained 400 on the second uninstall). 2026-11-09: hex-fiend/darwin (stuck pending on 636 in the afternoon install-delivery stall); since moved to 2026-11-09T16:00, so grammarly and zoom-rooms get one more pass too. 2026-11-10: grammarly-desktop, zoom-rooms and hex-fiend reran after 2026-11-09 16:00 (done); fellow/windows queued (uninstall left AppData\\Local\\Fellow on a congested 629, once). 2026-11-11: fellow/windows reran (635 pass 11-10 19:15; 629 install pending again); the last 8 macOS apps never covered queued so any host runs them, not only 631 (offline). 2026-11-11 later: aws-cli/windows queued once it stopped being a watcher resident (asana/windows replaced it), its first lifecycle cycle. 2026-11-16: all of the above reran after 2026-11-11 00:43 (done); python-3.13-arm64/windows queued: inventory never reported it after install on 629 (reproduced on retry, 2026-11-13); config arch routes it to an ARM host (863/864) to see whether it follows the app or the host.
rerun.why: second-host check: inventory never reported python-3.13-arm64 after install on 629

restart._doc: restarts.py: a Windows cycle whose install/uninstall output says a restart is needed (3010/1641/1610, Google Drive's 'restart the host') restarts the host through MDM, waits for its uptime to reset plus loop.settle_minutes, and reruns the app once; at most max_per_day per host, else the app is blocked on that host until it restarts. Only hosts listed here get restarted (all 8 soak VMs auto-login and boot without a BitLocker prompt, checked 2026-11-21); 863 restarted clean 2026-11-21 04:35Z (MDM ~5 min, auto-login); 861 (BitLocker, protection off) added for one harness-driven restart, then 859/862.
